links.reason: Kural 1265 wishes (காண்கமன்) and promises the pallor will go after seeing; Ainkurunuru 263 states it done in வந்தனன் வந்தன்று. The contrast of wish and fact is real but thin: both are the same punarthal situation of beauty returning with him.

Both bless the paalai road with coolness: ஞாயிறு காயாது ... தண்மழை தலைய வாகுக in Kuruntokai 378 and விசும்புடன் இருண்டு வெம்மை நீங்க ... இனிய ஆகுக தணிந்தே in Akananuru 283. The shift of speaker, friend before the elopement and செவிலி after it, is given by both thurais and makes a specific point.

The shared phrase பாரி பறம்பிற் பனிச்சுனைத் தெண்ணீர் is a real link, and Purananuru 176 does make it a thing scorned because near (ஓரூர் உண்மையின் இகழ்ந்தோர்). But Kuruntokai 196 gives the cause only as அற்றால் அன்பின் பாலே; the diagnosis of contempt bred by nearness is imported from the puram poem, not said by the friend.

The verbal echo இடிக்குங் கேளிர் / இடிக்குந் துணையார is exact. Kural 447 makes rebukers a ruler's safeguard; Kuruntokai 58 grants their aim (நிறுக்க லாற்றினோ நன்றுமற்று) and says the sickness has spread (பரந்தன்று) beyond checking, a genuine limit on the rule.

Both use குட்டுவன் மரந்தை அன்ன as a standard of a woman's beauty, a real puram name in akam similes. The teaches generalises from two instances to a 'neutral measure'; neither poet does more with Maranthai than borrow its fame.

The phrase புரோசு மயக்கி recurs (patikam 7 line 10, patikam 9 line 12), a real formula. But the claim of 'growing weight' over time assumes an order between the prefaces that nothing in them gives, and patikam 7 already has its வேள்வி; the phrase itself is obscure.

Purananuru 98: seeing the elephants, foes bar gates (மதிற் கதவம் எழுச் செல்லவும்); Patitruppattu 53: the elephant, seeing any gate (கதவுமெய் காணின்), cannot be held, so the king must avoid the forts his forebears guarded (முன்னோர் ஓம்பிய எயில்). The hyperbole is truly pushed a step further.

The shared scene is exact: உணங்கல்புள் ஒப்பும் / உணங்கற் படுபுள் ஓப்புதும். But Ainthinai Aimpathu 47's அணங்காகும் is the stock seizure by beauty; the claim that the fear comes from the brothers' presence is the marker's nuance, not the Tamil.

The stag (இரலை) with his doe appears in both rain scenes: தேடூஉ நின்ற இரலை ஏறே in 242, மடப் பிணை தழீஇய மா எருத்து இரலை in 256. The pairing is a shared image; in 256 the stag is part of the forest he gives up, so 'develops' overstates the relation.

Kural 1151's lever is her death (வாழ்வார்க் குரை); Natrinai 71's is his own leave-taking (கண்ணும் நுதலும் நீவி ... பிரிதல் வல்லிரோ). The contrast is real and specific, but neither verse limits the other, so the type is wrong.

Kural 81 makes household life exist for the guest (விருந்தோம்பி); Purananuru 395 shows the chief handing the bard to his wife with என்போல் போற்று, so the guest becomes a charge of the household. A rule and its instance with a specific added point.

Kural 1155's woman asks the friend to stop his going; Natrinai 124's friend begs him not to go (நீங்கல் வாழியர் ஐய). This is the same dissuasion situation; the teaches only says the friend carries it out, which is the shared topic.

Kuruntokai 313's யாத்தேம் யாத்தன்று நட்பே அவிழ்த்தற் கரிது does match Kural 791's நட்டபின் வீடில்லை. But nothing in the poem says the bond was entered without inquiry (நாடாது), so the teaches' conclusion is not shown.

Both men are struck by a woman likened to the divine: தாக்கணங்கு தானைக்கொண்டன்ன in the Kural, முருகு புணர்ந்து இயன்ற வள்ளி போல நின் உருவு கண் எறிப்ப in Natrinai 82. But Valli is a simile of beauty, not an attacker, so the claim that the Kural's divine attack is the hill's own deity stretches the poem; and neither qualifies the other.

Natrinai 313's millet has reached reaping (கொய்பதம் கொள்ளும்); Natrinai 306's reaping has begun (கொயல் தொடங்கினரே) and stubble (இருவி) stands. Both thurais give the same purpose (செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇயது), and the pair genuinely shows the stages.

Kalittokai 16 has virtue block his venture (அறன் ஓடி விலங்கின்று), and Kalittokai 150 says he left அறம் துறந்து: both treat going for wealth as against அறம, so they agree, not conflict. The split between staying and keeping faith (பொய்யார்) lies within 150 alone.

Akananuru 296 gives the plain fact (பெருநீர் வையை அவளொடு ஆடி, புலரா மார்பினை); Kalittokai 98's husband offers Vaigai bathing as alibi and the wife maps the flood onto a woman (அறல் for hair, கயல் for eyes). The pairing shows a specific turn.

The reed float is shared: புனலாடு மகளிர்க்குப் புணர்துணை உதவும் வேழம் in Ainkurunuru 15 and வேழத்துப் புணைதுணை யாகப் புனல்ஆடு கேண்மை in Akananuru 186. But in Ainkurunuru 15 it is a town epithet, not stated proof, and the two claims are not incompatible, so tension is the wrong type.

The konrai of the rains is the stock mullai sign in both. The friend's hope and the heroine's doubt (தோன்றுவர் தோன்றார், itself two-sided) are different responses to different situations, not a tension, and the conclusion about fixing the day is drawn by neither verse.

Both end on the decade's refrain எழுகமோ தெய்யோ; 235 sets it against பிரியலம் என்கமோ, and 236 names the goal நும்மூர்ச் செல்கம் with its causes (அன்னையும் அறிந்தனள் அலரும் ஆயின்று). Reading the open refrain by the next poem is accurate and specific.

The goad order is shared: முள் இட்டு ஊர்மதி and தீண்டா வை முள் தீண்டி. That Natrinai's never-used goad shows a convention behind Ainkurunuru's order is a modest inference; the link is chiefly a shared image, and the cited Ainkurunuru 485 is not in the packet.

Kural 1231's eyes are ashamed before flowers (நறுமலர் நாணின கண்); in Ainkurunuru 458 the rain-beaten konrai flowers come to resemble her wasted eyes (மாண்நலம் இழந்தஎன் கண்போன் றனவே). The reversal is real and specific, but it is a shared figure, not a qualification.

Purananuru 7 says the good things are gone (நல்ல இல்ல ஆகுபவால்) from others' rich lands of flood and fish; Porunararruppadai 218-231 shows Karikalan's own realm of mingled lands under ஒரு குடை. Same patron, and the pair names a specific two-sidedness of the praise.

The verbal tie is close: பூங்கட் புதல்வன் and மணிபுரை செவ்வாய் மார்பு in both poems. In Akananuru 66 the embrace of the son brings the husband home (மகனொடு தானே புகுதந்தோனே); in Kalittokai 79 the wife forbids it (புல்லல் எம் புதல்வனை) and calls the praise lies (பொய் பல பாராட்டி): the same gesture is given opposite worth.

Kuruntokai 31's ஆடுகள மகன் does echo Akananuru 236's ஆட்டன் அத்தி, but the identification with the legend rests on the colophon's poet name (ஆதிமந்தியார்), which the poem does not make. The teaches states as fact what is the tradition about the poem.

Kalittokai 81's son repeats words the street women taught (ஞாயர் பயிற்ற); Kainnilai 41's அறிந்தோம்யாம் ... மழலைச் சிறுவன் எனக்குடைமையால் then naturally reads as knowledge through the boy. A useful disambiguation, but it develops rather than qualifies.

Both invert temperature: நீங்கின் தெறூஉம் குறுகுங்கால் தண்ணென்னும் (Kural 1104) and வேனி லானே தண்ணியள் பனியே ... சிறுவெம் மையளே (Kuruntokai 376). The contrast of distance against season is accurate and teaches something.

The phrase is shared: நன்மனை நெடுநகர் புலம்புகொள / நன்னகர் புலம்ப. But in Ainkurunuru 236 the desolation is wrought by the north wind (இன்னா வாடை), not blamed on the mother's side, so 'each blames the empty house on the other side' misstates the friend; the type is also not qualification.

The unfired pot with water is distinctive and shared: பெயல்நீர்க் கேற்ற பசுங்கலம் and பசுமண் கலத்துள்நீர். In both the vessel is undone by what it holds, applied to love against counsel and to wealth by deceit: a meaningful shared image across domains.

Kural 183's புறங்கூறல் is slander behind one's back; Kural 1141's அலர் is the town's talk about lovers. Two different acts joined by the loose sense of 'gossip'; no incompatible claim, and the teaches is generic.

Kural 1151 demands to be told (எனக்குரை); Kuruntokai 207's man avoids telling because telling would stop him (செப்பினஞ் செலினே செலவரி தாகும்), and she hears it from others (சென்றெனக் கேட்ட நம் ஆர்வலர் பலரே). A genuine condition on the Kural's scene.

Akananuru 18's friend says outright பகல்நீ வரினும் புணர்குவை; Kuruntokai 141's heroine has the mother's errand reported (செல்கென் றோளே அன்னை) and the night refused (வாரலோ). The contrast of voices and how directly each can offer the day meeting is accurate.

Patitruppattu 70 has தொல்கடன் இறுத்த after gods by sacrifice and sages by learning; Kural 43 has ஐம்புலத்தாறு ஓம்பல். The debt against care contrast is real, but the Kural calls the five the chief duty, not 'equal claims', and a king's praise and a householder's rule are different settings.

Kural 1122's body-and-life bond and Kuruntokai 222's girl who follows every hold (தலைப்புணைக் கொளினே தலைப்புணைக் கொள்ளும்) share the topic of inseparability. The teaches only restates that topic as 'proved by action'.

Kural 913 calls the bought embrace false (பொருட்பெண்டிர் பொய்ம்மை முயக்கம்); in Paripadal 20 the courtesan says he paid (விலை தந்தான்) and he is the thief (அவன் கள்வன் கள்வி நான் அல்லேன்). A defensible tension, but it rests on an uncertain division of speakers and an obscure, gapped passage.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 20.74 has a lacuna, 72-74 are not in sangamtamil.com, and 82 கதுவாய் is obscure.

links.reason: Both have the cry on the vengai slope bring men running: புலிபுலி என்னும் பூசல் in 48 and the குறமகள் whose பூசல் is taken for an ஆகொள் வயப்புலி in 52. Both are disclosure poems (அறத்தொடு நிற்றல்), so the pairing of public alarm and the secret it starts is specific.

நாணிலான் சால்பும் ... நகை and நாணுடைமை ... அஃதின்றேல் பிணி agree that worth without shame fails. The claimed contrast, ridicule against a sickness of the man himself, is shaky, since பிணி in the couplet may be a trouble to onlookers; the item is one of five in the quatrain.

Ainkurunuru 131 limits the bond to a time when no கௌவை rises; Kural 1147's கௌவை is manure for her நோய், a complaint, not a welcome. Both lament gossip; there is no incompatible claim, and 'nourishment for her love' overstates the couplet.

Both are the man's debate with his heart, but Natrinai 262's colophon says he checked his departure (பிரிவிடை விலக்கியது), and its last line அரிது மன்றம்ம இன்மையது இளிவே is ambiguous. Different endings in two poems are not incompatible claims, and 'no fixed outcome' is generic.

The doe with fawn is shared: மறியுடை மான்பிணை / மறிஆடு மருங்கின் மடப்பிணை. But in Akananuru 34 what moves the man is the stag guarding the doe (துஞ்சுபுறம் காக்கும் பெருந்தகை), not the fawn; the claim of a sign calling him to 'wife and child' goes beyond both poems.

The opening formula செல்லா மோதில் சில்வளை விறலி is exact in both viraliyarruppadai poems. The difference is real: Purananuru 64 ends on leaving watery gruel (நெடுநீர்ப் புற்கை நீத்தனம்), Patitruppattu 57 on the king who fears suppliants' distress (இரவலர் புன்கண் அஞ்சும்) more than women's sulking.

Kural 1218 says on waking he moves into her heart (விழிக்குங்கால் நெஞ்சத்தர்); Kuruntokai 30's woman wakes, gropes the bed (அமளி தைவந்தனனே) and is தமியேன். On the plain readings they disagree on what waking after the dream is, a defensible tension.

Kuruntokai 17's rider is made a spectacle (மறுகின் ஆர்க்கவும் படுப); Natrinai 146 has kind people gather (அருளிக் கூடும் ஆர்வ மாக்கள்) and offer shade. The street's two faces is a real qualification, but the claim that this presses the girl's people to yield is convention, not said in either poem, and Natrinai 146's address is uncertain.

iraicchi.act: beats the rain bubbles on the wide rock with a small cane stick, breaking them
iraicchi.sense: as the monkey idly breaks fragile bubbles, the hill lord may carelessly ruin the beauty she asks him to keep by his grace

poems.note: The closing flower and homing birds are the evening's signs; only a match of mood with her grief.
The asunam simile is an open comparison joined by போல்.
The heron's cry is openly likened to the rewarded bard's chariot (பாணியின்).
The proverbs state their moral openly.
Pairs: the baited line for his tender courtship, the roe-laden carp killed for her undone by it.

iraicchi.act: tramples a path through the burning waste and goes on joined with its herd (குழுவொடு புணர்ந்து போம்)
iraicchi.sense: even the elephant takes its own with it through the fire, while the man would cross that waste and leave her

poems.note: The Bhima simile joins the elephant to an epic hero, not to the lovers, so the carrier stands.

Pairs: playing girls who scare the feeding birds for the new women who disturb her, the birds crying to their kin for her speaking her pain to the friend; the போல் joins the birds' cry to speech but not to a person of the poem.
The mocking cloud is the poem's own statement, made openly with போல.

iraicchi.act: the pregnant anril hen calls for her mate at midnight
iraicchi.sense: she too lies awake at midnight longing for the man who does not come

poems.note: Calling for a mate is close to a bare sound; it is taken as an act because the hen seeks the absent partner.
Line 2 is corrupt (dots in the base text), so the bird's role cannot be fully read.

iraicchi.act: the big vaalai seizes and keeps to its mate among the blue lilies
iraicchi.sense: the fish keeps its mate, while the town lord has sucked her beauty and cast her off like chewed cane

iraicchi.act: the buffalo cow, not leaving the calf the farmer has tied, grazes the paddy close by
iraicchi.sense: bound by her son as the cow by its calf, the wife stays in the house bearing its many duties

poems.note: The sea is addressed and openly likened to her (என்போல).
Her excuse to the mother carries the hidden sense: the sea for the shore lord, her sand-house for her ruined girlhood; it is a cover story, which makes the rule hard to apply.

vehicle: கொன்ற யானைச் செங் கோடு கழாஅ ... எழிலி
